As we approach Simchat Torah, we remember what happened to the Jewish world three years ago. We wept together on a day meant for joy, and we carry that grief into the holiday still.

In quieter, more personal ways, life teaches us how much a single moment can hold. A wedding where a parent's absence is felt in every embrace. The drive home after dropping a child at college, proud of who they are becoming and already missing who they were. Leaving a career you loved, grateful for the freedom ahead and grieving the life you built.

These feelings are difficult to untangle because they so often come from the same place. We miss people because we love them. 

We ache at an ending because what came before it mattered.

Perhaps there is beauty in allowing ourselves to feel all of it, without insisting that happiness be untroubled or that grief take up every room. We can dance with an ache in our hearts. There is room for the people we miss in the joy we still allow ourselves.

Shabbat Shalom. Wishing you a peaceful, restful weekend, and moments of joy you can welcome exactly as you are.

I use Claude. GPT. Grok. Gemini. Hermes. Grokbot. Even Dot now.

they’re all useful for different things.

however, the annoying thing I find is that I get really comfortable with a model, then something new drops in the OpenAI eco that I want to try, but the last 3 months I’ve mostly been using Claude? 

FUCK. I’m back to square one.

well the way to fix this is with a harness.

What’s a harness? a harness is everything you build around your model which makes them become replaceable.

You do this by giving it context, memory, instructions, skills, tools, workflows so whenever you go from Claude to GPT, or GPT to Gemini, or Gemini to Grok you’re giving everything your brain (model) needs.

here’s how I’d make one:

1. download Obsidian

Create a vault called MY-AI.
This is the folder every AI will eventually work from.

2. create PROFILE. md

Tell it who you are, your goals, interests, preferences + how you like to work.
Only include information that actually helps an AI work with you.

3. create AGENTS. md

This is your rulebook.
Add how you want AI to research, reason, write + behave.
Tell it to read PROFILE. md, CURRENT. md + check /Skills before starting a task.

4. create CURRENT .md

Keep your current projects, priorities + open questions here.
Keep it short and update it often.

5. create /Skills

Every prompt/process you repeatedly use becomes a skill:
crypto-research. md
challenge-thesis. md
Write the steps once. Improve them over time. Reuse them everywhere.

6. create /Memory

Save important:
> research
> decisions
> lessons
> outcomes
Your agents can now learn from what you’ve already done instead of starting from zero.

7: create /Projects

Give every important project its own folder + a short README.md explaining the goal, status + next steps.

8: connect it

Open the MY-AI folder in Codex, Claude Code, Cursor etc.
They now work from the same context, rules, skills + memory.

9: back it up

Put MY-AI in a private Git repo.
Now your entire harness is portable + version controlled.
